blocking_findings.title: Revoked independent verifier service root still produces acceptance and purpose authorization
blocking_findings.trigger: After ensureRuntimeVerifier validated the explicit service root, revoke that root before the child POST /acceptances. This is the same auth_principals.revoked transition used by Service.RevokePrincipal.
blocking_findings.observed: Two independent real Host/Mu/AppContainer/verifier.exe synthetic runs returned QUALIFIED_PURPOSE_AUTHORIZED after service-root revocation. The confirmation run logged SERVICE_ROOT_REVOKE rows=1 and returned a real server AcceptanceReceipt plus AVAILABLE runtime reference and mu_turn purpose. Synthetic provider call count remained 1 per reproduction; actual model calls were 0.
blocking_findings.why: The new flow issues a credential to the child and later authorizes purpose without requiring the service-root principal to remain active. authenticate checks only the child; acceptance and qualificationEvidence obtain authorityRoot but compare identifiers without testing root revocation. A revoked service can therefore complete the new qualification chain. The repository already treats active authority-root state as necessary for other execution review evidence (change_impact.go:65-70).
source_chain: internal/domain/auth.go:63-70 root-only revocation and child-only authentication
internal/domain/runtime_admission.go:109-138 child role/grant check plus root identity comparison
blocking_findings.suggestion: Bind the managed verifier child to its installed service registration and require the service root to be current and unrevoked inside authoritative acceptance snapshots and qualification/current-admission/purpose transactions. Do not rely solely on another host preflight; that leaves the acceptance race. Preserve the existing application-separation/holdout distinction and add root-revocation tests before acceptance, before qualify/purpose, and on subsequent use.
blocking_findings.status: REPRODUCED_BLOCKER; original frozen source not changed

review_facts: All 15 candidate source files match Git objects and frozen bytes. All 17 frozen author evidence hashes match. Both actual binaries match frozen hashes and go version -m reports exact candidate and vcs.modified=false. Total 34 checked members; source worktree remains clean.

The managed control startup owns or borrows the original data-root lease and refuses a second coordinator. Qualification joins scanMu, active executor tracking, workers, existing Begin gates and RunAdmitted. Durable request-consumption and original task state deny automatic replay.

The prior phase1 exact-count grant defect is repaired narrowly: base project grant required; qualification grants bind original task/run/epoch, normal Mu grants bind original dispatch/profile/Owner purpose. Foreign/task-only/missing/wrong/restricted grants fail. Host integration independently proves renewed reconciliation after both original qualification and ordinary mu_turn.

Verifier installation is explicit local administrative authority. Runtime verifies bytes and observes actual PID, creation time and image hash, then nonce handshake over inherited private pipes. Declared SourceCommit is not an OS provenance proof; actual frozen executables were separately verified using Go build metadata. Test manifest uses a declared zero commit and is not claimed as production installation provenance.

The service root is explicitly registered and differs from Owner/executor lineage; root has no grants or credential. Child has only project VERIFIER. This is application separation, not OS isolation or protected holdout. The blocker is continuous root revocation after registration.

The short child credential is issued only after execution settles, transferred in a private pipe rather than argv/environment/files/logs/renderer/coordinator, and revoked on normal or rejected acceptance paths. Child re-reads sealed artifacts and current Task/Run via API, checks the private snapshot and asks existing server to recompute acceptance.

UNKNOWN validation is limited to credential-free numeric loopback MODEL with null max_cost. It checks original UNKNOWN/null amount/null reservation, exact key/event/run/time/request hash, one ledger row, complete current budget ancestry and every ancestor UNLIMITED_AMOUNT with ALLOW_AND_RECORD. Both server snapshots include sorted current policies. Existing bounded RESERVE branch remains unchanged.

Independent negative acceptance tests prove child revocation and budget policy drift prevent PASS and AVAILABLE, preserve the original UNKNOWN/null row, revoke temporary verifier credentials and prevent another model dispatch. The service-root revocation counterexample fails the same expected boundary.
